I am an undergraduate student at the University of Waterloo interested in empirical software engineering, developer tools, and software testing. I study how software artifacts are created, reused, and maintained, and I build tools for research workflows.

Through UR2PhD, I am currently examining reuse patterns in the GitSkills dataset. I will also join Professor Ho Chen's group at the University of Hong Kong remotely, working with Huaien Zhang. That work may involve compiler testing and analyzing GitHub issues.

Current focus: AI agent skill reuse, repository history, and empirical methods for studying software evolution.

Research Interests

My current research centers on the reuse of AI agent skills across public repositories. I am interested in what exact content matches can show, what repository history adds, and how the quality of a skill could be evaluated with meaningful measures.

  • Skill reuse and evolution: identifying identical content across repositories and studying how copies change over time.
  • Evidence of origin: using timestamps and commit history carefully; identical files alone do not establish who copied from whom.
  • Software quality: considering multiple observable signals rather than treating popularity or copy count as a complete measure of usefulness.

Dataset reference: GitSkills: A Dataset of Agent Skills on GitHub.
